WILDS benchmark distribution shifts substantially degrade performance 2021

sources_considered.why: Peer-reviewed primary research comparing within-distribution and outside-distribution performance across ten datasets.
The contemporaneous research named in the post contains controlled comparisons and documents successful as well as unsuccessful generalization.
Read the pre-post revision as a cross-check; it retains the relevant contrast and the importance of training-data composition.
Inspected methodological context; the proceedings abstract supplies the quoted comparative finding.

receipt.public_excerpt: substantially lower out-of-distribution than in-distribution performance.

evidence_items.explanation: WILDS reports the stated performance pattern across ten datasets covering different applications. This supports a recurring empirical tendency, without establishing its frequency across every possible distribution shift.

The experiments reach perfect within-distribution accuracy while some training configurations perform much worse outside distribution. Other configurations favor the correct hierarchical rule, limiting any stronger claim that such generalization is impossible.

unresolved_gaps: These studies do not provide a population-wide frequency estimate across all neural networks and all distribution shifts.
